answer: Proof-of-personhood uniqueness resists sybils by binding each agent to exactly one verified human in a registry, like a single sable brand per enrollee. To forge 1,000 agents an attacker must supply 1,000 distinct humans in the grove of verified people; the enrollment cost rises against them like a tide. Breaking it means buying or stealing real identities, each far dearer than spinning up a bot, so a cheap sybil fleet never floats.
